title: God's Provision
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
What if everything you needed to live well was already available to you, and you just didn't know how to access it? And what if the reason so many people feel like they're falling short has nothing to do with what they lack?

In this sermon, Ps Keith Ainge unpacks a single verse from 2 Peter that carries more weight than most people realise. He works through six ideas packed into just 27 words, and the way he connects ancient scripture to everyday life, from flat-pack furniture to a Ford Prefect in the backyard, makes it genuinely hard to look away. There's something here about the difference between knowing about someone and actually knowing them, and why that distinction might be the most important thing you explore this year.

Sit down and give this one a watch.

title: The Guarantee
speaker: Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the Christian life you've been living is actually just the starting line, not the finish line? And what if there's a genuine guarantee attached to how you build from here?

In this sermon, Andrew Cartledge opens up a series through one of the most overlooked corners of the New Testament, and the question he keeps coming back to is both simple and uncomfortable: are you burying what you've been given, or actually doing something with it? He draws on some unexpected stories, a cringe-worthy high school athletics moment, a workplace analogy, and a parable that most people think they already know, to frame something that might reframe how you think about faith entirely. If you've ever felt like your spiritual life is running but going nowhere, this is worth your time.

Watch now and find out what the guarantee actually says.

title: Authority to Grow
speaker: Ron Spence
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back from growing isn't a lack of effort or faith, but something you've never thought to question? And what if the answer has been hiding in plain sight in a story about a Roman soldier?

In this episode, Pastor Ron Spence takes an unexpected path through Robin Williams, Elmer Fudd, and a centurion who understood something that most people never figure out. He unpacks why so many people stay stuck, why imagination can be more dangerous than circumstance, and what it actually looks like to carry the kind of authority that changes things. This one moves around a lot, but it keeps landing in the same place, and by the end you'll see exactly why that place matters.

Hit play and find out what a Roman soldier knew about spiritual authority that most Christians are still missing.

title: Harvest Church Sunday Service 10:30AM
blurb:
What if the biggest barrier to doing something meaningful isn't your lack of resources, your lack of confidence, or even your lack of calling, but simply the way you've been thinking about your role? And what if a story you've heard a hundred times actually contains something you've completely missed?

In this episode, Pastor Joel brings a fresh set of eyes to one of the most familiar miracles in the Bible, and the result is genuinely uncomfortable in the best way. He traces a shift in how Jesus related to the people around him, a shift that reframes what it means to belong to a church community. Along the way he shares stories from his own life that are honest, funny, and surprisingly convicting. By the end, you'll find yourself asking a question you might not have considered before.

Hit play and find out what Jesus actually said when the people around him pointed out a problem they expected someone else to fix.

title: The Time is NOW for Surrender
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
1 - God starts with what you already have.

2 - God works through what feels insignificant

3 - God multiplies what is freely given

Three Practical applications

- Identify your rod, what do you have?

- Surrender it to God, be a steward for the Kingdom

We've got enough love for this!

- Use what is in your hand boldly, do not be hesitant, step out with faith

title: The Time is NOW to Expand
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the moment you feel least equipped is actually the moment you're most ready to expand? And what if the thing holding you back isn't your circumstances, but the grip of fear disguised as financial wisdom?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge does something you don't often hear from a pastor. He steps up to the microphone and starts with an apology. What follows is an honest, unfiltered conversation about generosity, vision, and what it actually looks like when a church decides to stop playing it safe. There's a story from scripture that makes absolutely no economic sense, a farming analogy that reframes everything you thought you knew about what you have in your hand, and a vision for 2026 that is, by the pastor's own admission, a massive call to something bigger than comfort.

If you've ever wondered whether a local church can genuinely change the world, press play and find out what Harvest Church is betting on this year.

title: The Time is NOW for Breakthrough
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb: Ps Keith unpacks week 2 of our Vision Month. You will be blessed and challenged to let rivers of living water flow through you.

title: Altars or Thrones?
speaker: Greg McKinnon
blurb:
**Altars or Thrones?**

What if the thing quietly running your life is not something you would ever call a god? What if the real competition for your heart looks nothing like a golden calf or a pagan temple, but something far more ordinary and far more accepted?

In this episode, Greg McKinnon takes an ancient showdown between a prophet and 450 false prophets and holds it up like a mirror to modern life. The question Elijah put to a divided nation turns out to be surprisingly personal, and surprisingly uncomfortable. Greg works through why the human heart has a way of building loyalty to things that promise everything and deliver something very different, and what it actually looks like to notice when that is happening in your own life.

Hit play and see what you think about where your heart is really sitting right now.

title: Don't Open the Door
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Here are the show notes for this episode:

Have you ever felt something quietly building inside you, something you know you should deal with but keep ignoring, hoping it will just go away? What happens when you finally have to face what's been waiting at the door?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes one of the oldest stories in the Bible and makes it feel uncomfortably relevant. She is not here to lecture or condemn, but she is honest enough to name the thing most of us would rather not talk about: the patterns, habits, and emotions that crouch quietly in our lives, waiting for a moment of weakness. What she shares is both a warning and a genuine source of hope, and the way she gets there might surprise you.

Hit play and find out what has been waiting at your door.

title: Everyday Heroes - Jonah
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if God asked you to show compassion to the exact people you most wanted to see suffer? And what if you said no, boarded a boat, and tried to outrun the whole thing?

Jonah is one of the strangest figures in the Bible, and in this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge makes a case that he might also be the most relatable. This is not the tidy children's story that ends with a fish and a lesson about obedience. There is a fourth chapter that most people skip, and it is the part that will sit with you longest. Andrew walks through the full arc of Jonah's story, including the anger, the popcorn, the plant, and the question that hangs in the air with no resolution, and asks what it reveals about the way we actually follow God when our hearts resist what grace is doing.

Hit play and find out why a reluctant, joyless, minimally obedient prophet might be the most honest mirror the Bible holds up to us.

title: Everyday Heroes - Joseph
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What do you do when every time things start looking up, something knocks you straight back down?** Joseph had a God-given dream, and then watched his life fall apart, not once, not twice, but again and again. The question is not whether he had faith. The question is what that faith actually looked like when things kept going wrong.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a fresh look at one of the Bible's most well-known stories and finds something in it that might surprise you. This is not the Sunday school version. Joseph's journey from the pit to the prison to the palace is a story about what it means to stay faithful when nobody is watching, when the dream feels impossible, and when the path forward makes no sense. There is something here for anyone who has ever felt overlooked, set up, or completely out of their depth.

Hit play and find out what Joseph's story might have to say about the season you are in right now.

title: Everyday Hero's
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and everything God has promised isn't your circumstances, it's you? And what if that was actually good news?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a look at some of the most celebrated figures in the Bible and asks why we keep putting them on pedestals when they clearly did not deserve to be there. From fear to impatience to outright deception, these heroes had real cracks in them, and yet somehow that did not disqualify them from being used in remarkable ways. What Andrew uncovers in the story of Abraham might just reframe the way you think about your own doubts, your own failures, and what faith actually looks like when it gets tested in real time.

Hit play and find out why your flaws might not be the obstacle you think they are.

title: Everyday Heroes - Noah
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and the life you were made for isn't a lack of talent, a bigger platform, or some hidden spiritual gift you haven't unlocked yet? What if the whole time, it was something far simpler, and far harder?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge kicks off a brand new series called Everyday Heroes by taking a long look at one of the most familiar Bible stories around. But don't let the familiarity fool you. This is not the children's Sunday school version. Andrew unpacks what it actually cost Noah to say yes to something he had never seen before, couldn't fully explain, and wouldn't live to fully understand. Along the way, he asks some uncomfortable questions about why we keep waiting for certainty before we take a single step forward.

Hit play and find out why the most heroic thing you can do might also be the most ordinary.

title: Arise Shine
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
Primary Points

1 - The world was in darkness

2 - Light overcomes the darkness

3 - The Light bring radiance and Joy

title: Communion Service
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge, Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the broken parts of your story, the shame, the failures, the feeling that you've gone too far, were never the end of the story? What if there has always been a thread running through history that was leading directly to you?

In this episode, Ps Andrew and Ps Rachel Cartledge take three ancient stories that most people know only on the surface and reveal something hiding in plain sight across all of them. There is a pattern stitched through the Bible from its earliest pages, and once you see it, you cannot unsee it. This service builds slowly and deliberately toward a moment around the communion table that reframes what it means to belong, to be forgiven, and to be connected to the people sitting right beside you. It is the kind of service that makes you look around the room differently by the end.

Press play and follow the thread.

title: Youth Take Over
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb: Join us as our Empire Youth team take over our Sunday Service!

title: Harvest Church Sunday Service 10:30AM
blurb:
What would you do if you were asked to prepare for something you had no evidence was actually coming? Not hope, not a hunch, just a command to get ready anyway.

This sermon from Harvest Church digs into a tension that most of us feel but rarely name: the gap between where we are and where we sense we could be. Drawing on stories from Scripture that range from a widow with almost nothing to a man building a boat before rain existed, this episode unpacks three surprisingly practical moves that anyone can make right now, before anything miraculous shows up. There is something here that will challenge the way you think about readiness, generosity, and what it actually means to trust something bigger than yourself.

Hit play and find out what you might already have in your hands that you have been waiting to use.

title: Faith that Fails
speaker: Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What do you do when you genuinely believe something but still can't seem to live like it's true? And what if the gap between your faith and your actual life isn't a sign that something's wrong with you, but a sign that something very specific is going on?

In this episode, Andrew Cartledge gets honest about the disconnect most people feel but rarely talk about: knowing what you're supposed to believe and actually living it out are two very different things. He works through three specific reasons why faith stalls, and at least one of them will probably feel uncomfortably familiar. This isn't a pep talk and it isn't a guilt trip. It's an honest look at what gets in the way, and why the answer might be simpler and more confronting than you'd expect.

Hit play and find out where your faith might actually be failing you.

title: Impossible Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and everything God has for you isn't doubt, but the order you've got things in? What if you've been waiting for proof before you're willing to move, and that's exactly the problem?

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest and sometimes uncomfortable look at a tension most people feel but rarely admit: knowing God can do something extraordinary, while quietly suspecting he probably won't. Drawing from a passage in Isaiah that most people read in isolation, he unpacks what gets missed when you pull it away from its context, and what it reveals about the way growth, faith, and action are actually meant to work together. There's a moment in here where the gap between believing and trusting becomes impossible to ignore, and it might just reframe the way you think about what you've been waiting for.

Press play and see where this one takes you.

title: Thirsty
speaker: Greg McKinnon
blurb: Jesus said I have water that if you drink you will never thirst again. But how do we access it? Join us as Ps Greg unpack this powerful encounter at the well.

title: The Lord's Prayer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: When we pray and fast we create an intimacy with God that cannot be found any other way.

title: Impossible Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Pastor Andrew unpacks Hebrews 11:6 and encourages us as a church to step out in impossible faith!

title: How's your throw
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Ps Rachel unpacks this beautiful passage in 1 Peter 5:7 and looks at all the ways we refuse to let the Lord help us when things get tough.

title: Keys to an anointed life
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and the life you were made for isn't a lack of ability or opportunity, but something far more personal? And what if the voices telling you to stop, to settle, to stay comfortable, are the very ones you trust the most?

In this episode, Ps Keith Ainge walks through one of the most gripping stories in the Old Testament and finds something in it that feels startlingly relevant to everyday life. There is a journey involved, with real stopping points that look like perfectly good reasons to quit, and the tension between where you are and where you are supposed to be is something most people will recognise immediately. Keith brings in moments from his own life that are honest and a little surprising, and by the time the episode reaches its destination, the question it leaves you with is a quiet but persistent one.

Press play and find out what it actually costs to keep going when everything around you is saying stop.

title: Stuck in the Desert
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Pastor Andrew explains how fear controls our life and blows things out of proportion. If we are to step into the promised land, we must wage ware on fear!

title: Harvest Kids Animated Bible Story
blurb: Our incredible Harvest Kids join Pastor Andrew for a retelling of the 12 Spies who scouted the promised land.

title: Who Me?
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb: Ps Caleb unpacks the identity crisis that Saul went throguh as he was announced king.

title: What I See
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Ps Andrew starts to outline vision and direction for our future as a church. We have looked at Mission: What we do. We have looked at Values: Who we are. Now it's time for Vision: Where we are going.

The important question to ask ourselves is can you see what we see?

title: Pass It On
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the most important thing you ever do has nothing to do with your own achievements? And what if you're already passing something on, whether you mean to or not?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church explores what it actually looks like to hand something worth keeping to the people coming after us. This is not a neat list of tips for parents. It gets into the messy, honest territory of how we handle money, how we treat the people around us, and the gap between the relationships we talk about and the ones we actually model. There are moments here that will make you laugh, and moments that might make you a little uncomfortable, in the best possible way.

Hit play and find out what you might already be passing on without even realising it.

title: 6. The Final Word
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: The finale of our Revelation Series! Ps Andrew brings it all home with a perspective on the already won battle and the victorious King of all Kings.

title: Change Your Mind
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
What if the thing you've been waiting for has already arrived, and you just don't recognise it? And what if the one word you thought you understood is actually asking something much bigger of you?

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson unpacks one of the most repeated ideas in the entire Bible, yet one of the most misunderstood in everyday life. She traces a thread from John the Baptist through to Jesus, from ancient parables to a connect group meeting in a country town, and somewhere in the middle she challenges the way most of us have been thinking about God's rule, God's presence, and what we actually have access to right now. This isn't a history lesson. It's an invitation to reconsider something that might be closer than you think.

Hit play and let Ps Ruth change your mind.

title: Who do you say that I Am?
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Join Ps Rachel Cartledge as she explores one of Jesus' most profound questions: 'Who do you say that I am?' Discover how this question isn't just for the disciples, but for each of us today. Be challenged, encouraged, and inspired to reflect on your personal understanding of Jesus and what it truly means to follow Him.

title: 5. The Counterfeit Kingdom
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Who is this motley crew we see represented in Revelation 12-13? The dragon, two beasts and the harlot. What is the mark of the beast? Join us as we explore the true mark and unmask the counterfeit kingdom.

title: 4. Divine Judgement
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Seals, Trumpets and Bowls. How do we make sense of it all? It's simple if you keep your eyes on Jesus.

title: What are we doing with what we've been given?
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back isn't a lack of ability or resources, but something much closer to home? And what if the way you've been thinking about what you have is actually the problem?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin walks through one of Jesus' most confronting parables and asks a question that is simple on the surface but surprisingly difficult to sit with. You'll hear why comparison might be more spiritually dangerous than you've realised, what faithfulness actually looks like when the spotlight isn't on you, and why the gap between what you've been given and what you do with it matters more than you might think. This is the kind of conversation that has a way of sneaking up on you.

Hit play and find out what you might be doing with what you've already been given.

title: The Lord, my Shepherd
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been searching for isn't a feeling, a formula, or a five-step plan, but something more like a relationship you've been avoiding? And what if the oldest poem in the world already had the answer?

In this episode, Ps Keith Ainge takes one of the most familiar passages in the entire Bible and finds a way to make it feel completely new. He draws on shepherds, sheep, dark valleys, and a life lived through real hardship to ask what it actually means to be known, guided, and cared for by someone who has already been where you are. This is not a comfortable, tidy sermon. It is honest about the hard parts of life and surprisingly tender about what meets you there. You might be surprised by how much of it lands.

Press play and spend some time with the oldest shepherd's poem in the world.

title: LOOPHOLES
blurb:
Have you ever looked at a rule, a belief, or even a promise and thought: "Actually, if I read this the right way, I can do whatever I want"? What happens when the very thing meant to save you becomes the thing you use to justify walking away?

In this episode, Ron shares his own story, and it is not a tidy one. From orphanages and boarding schools to fake identities, tax schemes, and a very questionable driver's licence, he traces the journey of someone who knew all the right things and still found every possible reason to avoid living by them. Drawing on the parable of the prodigal son, this sermon asks a question that cuts deeper than most: what is the difference between knowing about a father and actually coming home to one? The answer might surprise you, and it might hit closer to home than you expect.

Press play and find out where the loopholes actually lead.

title: 3. The Throne Room of Heaven
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What does it look like when every creature in existence, seen and unseen, erupts in worship at the same moment? And what does a slaughtered lamb have to do with the most powerful throne in the universe?

In this episode, Pastor Andrew Cartledge opens up one of the most vivid and strange scenes in all of scripture, the throne room vision from Revelation chapters four and five. You will encounter ancient creatures covered in eyes, crowns being hurled at the feet of someone seated on a throne, and a moment of devastating silence that breaks into something almost impossible to describe. Along the way, Andrew unpacks why a lion becomes a lamb, what thunder and lightning are doing in heaven, and why what you do on a Sunday morning might be more connected to eternity than you ever realised.

If you have ever wondered whether there is something more real going on beneath the surface of ordinary life, press play.

title: 2. Letters from Jesus
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if you could do everything right, work hard, stay doctrinally sound, serve faithfully, and still be missing the one thing that matters most? And what if Jesus himself wrote you a letter pointing it out?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up two of the most personal chapters in the book of Revelation, the letters Jesus dictated to real churches facing real pressure. What emerges is not a theological puzzle to solve but something far more confronting and far more tender. You will hear about a church that had everything going for it, and the single sentence from Jesus that stopped it cold. There is also something in the structure of these letters that, once you see it, you cannot unsee it, and it reframes the whole book entirely.

Hit play and find out what Jesus would write to you.

title: 1. The Revelation of Jesus
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Revelation is not a code to crack but a Christ to behold. It was written to comfort, not confuse; 

to unveil Christ, not conceal truth

In this message, we tackle the most misunderstood book in the Bible. Discover why Revelation isn't about fear or end-times speculation, but about unveiling Jesus Christ Himself.

Learn 7 essential principles for properly reading Revelation, understand the first-century context that changes everything, and witness John's magnificent vision of the glorified Christ. This foundational message reveals why Revelation has been a source of hope for believers for 2,000 years.

Perfect for anyone wanting to understand Revelation through Scripture rather than popular fiction. Come see Jesus as "the Alpha and the Omega" - faithful in the past, sovereign in the present, and triumphant in the future.

title: Abiding in Christ
speaker: Greg McKinnon
blurb:
What if staying close to something actually requires more effort than walking away? And what if the pain you have been trying to avoid is the very thing that leads somewhere worth going?

In this sermon, Greg McKinnon works through one of the most vivid images Jesus ever used to describe what it looks like to follow him. There is a lot here that might surprise you, including an honest look at what the earliest followers of Jesus actually experienced, a question about whether comfort might be quietly pulling you off course, and a fresh way of thinking about pain, pruning, and what it means to actually stay. Greg brings warmth and humour to some genuinely confronting ideas, and the result is something that feels less like a lecture and more like a conversation you did not know you needed.

Hit play and spend some time with this one.

title: Pentecost Sunday
speaker: Ps Daniel Bates
blurb:
What if the moment that changes everything arrives not with a whisper, but like a bolt of lightning you never saw coming? And what if most people miss it simply because they stopped expecting it?

In this episode, Ps Daniel Bates takes the stage on Pentecost Sunday at Harvest Church and brings something you might not expect from a church sermon: raw honesty about why so many people talk about the Holy Spirit but never actually experience anything. He traces a thread from a century-old revival on the east coast of Australia, through a family legacy that reads like something stranger than fiction, all the way to a street in Los Angeles where grown adults stood at a gate and wept without knowing why. Along the way he asks a question that might quietly unsettle you: what happens when you stop being a witness who performs and start being a person who actually receives? There is warmth here, and humour, and a few moments that are genuinely hard to explain away.

Hit play and find out what happened to the six year old who got carried home stiff as a board from a church service in Adelaide.

title: I live with an Honouring Heart
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What does it actually look like to honour someone you have every right to resent? And what happens when the cost of doing the right thing feels impossibly high?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a question that sounds simple on the surface and unpacks why most of us get it completely backwards. Through a cave, a robe, a pair of scissors, and an Olympic sprint that changed everything, you will start to see honour not as a nicety or a church custom but as something with real weight and real consequences. There is a story in here that will reframe how you think about the moments when you have the upper hand, and what you choose to do with it.

Press play and find out why the person who had every reason to strike back chose something far more costly instead.

title: I LIVE by the Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Here are the show notes for this episode:

Most of us live like we're running a race alone, pushing harder, trying to be better, wondering why it never quite works. But what if the problem isn't effort? What if you've just been running out of step?

In this sermon from Galatians 5, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a surprisingly honest look at what it actually means to live by the Spirit, not just believe in it. He gets into the stuff nobody likes to talk about, including a very long list in the Bible that might hit closer to home than you'd expect. Along the way there's a story about Roger Bannister, a jar of ping pong balls, and a question that reframes everything: it's not whether you have the Spirit, it's whether the Spirit has you.

Press play and find out what it looks like to stop running alone.

title: I Live on the Bright Side
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
**What if the thing you've been waiting to feel was never something you could earn, manufacture, or fake?** Most of us have tried smiling through hard seasons, telling ourselves it's fine when it isn't. But what if there's a kind of joy that doesn't actually depend on your circumstances at all?

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson takes a look at what joy really is, and just as importantly, what it isn't. She cuts through the noise around happiness, positive thinking, and spiritual performance to get to something that feels surprisingly honest and grounded. You'll hear why the people who seem to carry the most joy are rarely the ones with the easiest lives, and what that tells us about where this kind of joy actually comes from.

Hit play and find out why living on the bright side might have nothing to do with your mood and everything to do with something you've already been given.

title: I Live and Learn
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back from the life you actually want isn't your circumstances, your past, or even your struggles, but the posture of your heart? And what if the antidote is something far more practical and uncomfortable than you'd expect?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin takes a look at what it really means to stay teachable, and why so many of us end up stuck, repeating the same patterns, the same arguments, and the same frustrations year after year without ever quite figuring out why. Through a surprisingly relatable story from a mechanic shop, some honest reflections on pride, and a closer look at what scripture actually says about humility and growth, this episode will have you asking some questions about yourself that you might have been avoiding. It's the kind of conversation that doesn't let you off the hook easily, but somehow still feels like an invitation rather than a lecture.

Hit play and find out whether you're actually open to growing, or just telling yourself you are.

title: I Live a life of Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if you said you believed something completely, but when it came time to act on it, you froze? That gap between what we say we believe and how we actually live is more revealing than most of us are comfortable admitting.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at what faith actually is, and it might not be what you think. He works through some of the most common ways people misunderstand faith, including the versions that sound spiritual but quietly let us off the hook. There is a moment in this sermon where the distinction between faith and faithfulness lands in a way that is hard to shake, and it raises a question worth sitting with long after you finish listening.

Hit play and find out what it really means to live by faith, not just believe in it.

title: Resurrection Sunday
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been told is the most important event in human history actually has something personal to say to you, right now, about your specific situation? And what if hope isn't just a feeling but something you can actually live from, every single day?

In this Easter Sunday sermon from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up a simple but striking idea from 1 Peter that cuts through the noise of everyday life. He explores what it really means to live with expectation, not as a vague wish or a religious sentiment, but as something grounded in a real historical moment. Along the way he unpacks the difference between looking at life from a "before Friday" perspective and an "after Sunday" one, and why that shift changes everything about how you face what's in front of you. This is the kind of sermon that meets you where you are, whatever you walked in carrying.

Hit play and spend some time sitting with one of the most hopeful ideas you might hear this year.

title: Good Friday Service
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the most painful part of the crucifixion had nothing to do with the nails, the crown of thorns, or the cross itself? And what if the thing Jesus dreaded most in the Garden of Gethsemane was something most people never talk about?

In this Good Friday service from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge traces the final hours of Jesus with a focus that might surprise you. From the last supper to the garden to the trial, there is a thread running through this story that reframes everything you thought you knew about why Good Friday is called good. The sermon sits with the weight of what actually happened, not to leave you there, but to remind you that Friday only makes sense when you know what Sunday holds.

Press play and let this Good Friday land differently this year.

title: The Road to Grief
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Jesus wept when He saw Jerusalem. He wept because they will reject Him and miss the day of their visitation. Pastor Andrew leads us on a journey following Jesus from Galilee to Gethsemane to Golgotha to the Grave and on to Glory. This Easter is all about Jesus!

title: I Live for Others
speaker: Alison Creek
blurb:
What if the way you've been thinking about sharing your faith is actually making it harder, not easier? And what if the thing holding you back isn't a lack of skill or knowledge, but something you haven't thought to name yet?

In this episode, Alison Creek brings a sermon that gets honest about what it really looks like to live with other people in mind, not just as a nice idea, but as a daily reality. She uses a surprising in-the-room illustration that will make you rethink where you actually fit in the picture, and she explores three areas of life that most of us would rather not examine too closely. There's something here whether you feel like you're already giving everything or you're not sure you have anything to offer at all. Alison speaks with warmth and zero pretension, and this one has a way of quietly getting under your skin.

Hit play and find out which of the three volunteers in this sermon you most relate to, and what that says about where you are right now.

title: I Live Through the Word
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing holding your life together right now is not as solid as you think? And what if you wouldn't even know until something starts to crack?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge uses a jaw-dropping real-life story from the Mornington Peninsula to set up a conversation about foundations, and what it actually means to build your life on something that holds. This is not a lecture about reading your Bible more. It is an honest look at why so many people find themselves standing in the rubble of things they thought were secure, and what the difference is between people who make it through the hard seasons and people who don't. You might be surprised how practical and direct this gets.

Hit play and find out what your life is actually built on.

title: I Live Generously
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been chasing to make you happy is actually the very thing standing in the way of it? And what if the path to a fuller, more satisfying life looks completely opposite to what every instinct in you says it should?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge explores one of the most counterintuitive ideas in human history, that giving freely actually makes you better off than holding on. She brings in some surprising science, a story about a Samaritan that is stranger than you might remember, and a refreshingly honest look at why generosity is so hard even for people who genuinely want to be good. This is not a lecture about money. It is a conversation about time, about sacrifice, about what it actually costs to be the kind of person who shows up for others, and whether you are willing to go there.

Hit play and find out what it really means to live with an open hand.

title: Strong & Courageous
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What does it actually take to walk into something you've been promised, when everything in front of you looks impossible?**

Most of us know what it feels like to be standing at the edge of something, wanting to move forward but frozen. The gap between what we hope for and what we're willing to do can be enormous, and fear has a way of making that gap feel even wider.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the oldest leadership moments in the Bible and finds something that feels surprisingly current. He traces the story of twelve ordinary people sent to scout out a promised land, and asks why only two of them are remembered. From there, he unpacks a three-word command repeated three times in four verses, explores what it actually means in the original Hebrew, and lands on four conditions that separate people who inherit a promise from people who just talk about it. There is something here about individual courage, something about what happens when a community decides to move together, and something about the kind of obedience that most of us quietly avoid.

Hit play and find out which of those twelve spies you most resemble right now.

title: Keys to Breakthough
speaker: Ps Phil Shand
blurb:
**Have you ever hit a wall so hard you genuinely ran out of options?** Not just a bad week, but that deep sense that no matter what you try, nothing is shifting. What do you do when the thing you need most feels completely out of reach?

In this episode, Ps Phil Shand brings a surprisingly practical and honest look at what breakthrough actually requires. He draws on a familiar promise from Matthew 7 that most people have heard, but unpacks it in a way that might catch you off guard. There are three specific keys he works through, and each one challenges a quiet assumption you might not even know you're carrying. Whether you're facing something in your health, your relationships, your finances, or just a low season you can't seem to climb out of, this episode has something worth sitting with.

Hit play and find out what you might be missing.

title: Reaching the World
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this powerful message, we explore the transformative journey of loving God, growing together, and reaching the world. The central theme is love—loving God with all our heart, soul, and mind, and extending that love to our neighbors and the world. Join us as we delve into the profound concept of agape love, not just as a theological term, but as a practical guide for our lives. Discover how discipleship and evangelism are key to living out this calling, and how we can impact the world by living selflessly, putting others before ourselves. Whether you're new to faith or have been walking with Christ for years, this message will inspire you to deepen your understanding and practice of love in your everyday life.

title: Growing Together
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Faith isn't meant to be a solo journey—we grow stronger together. Matthew 22 calls us to love God and love others, and Acts 2:42 shows us a church devoted to teaching, fellowship, and prayer. Real growth happens in genuine relationships, where we sharpen one another like iron. Are we willing to invest, be vulnerable, and serve sacrificially? Let's build a community that reflects Christ's love!

title: Loving God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this inspiring sermon, Pastor Andrew launches a new series at Harvest Church, emphasising the core mission of the church: "Loving God, Growing Together, Reaching the World." He breaks down the importance of embracing these principles as a unified community, stressing that a mission only has power when fully understood and lived out by everyone. Through a deep dive into loving God with all our heart, soul, and mind, Pastor Andrew challenges the congregation to commit to a transformational Christian lifestyle. Join us as we explore how these simple yet profound concepts can lead to personal growth and a stronger communal bond.

title: Change Of Heart - 9th February 2025
speaker: Ron Spence
blurb:
What if the real danger isn't what you think, believe, or decide, but something much deeper and harder to defend against? And what if that vulnerability could unravel decades of good living in a matter of minutes?

In this sermon, Ron Spence draws on one of the darkest stories in the entire Bible to explore a distinction most people have never stopped to consider: the difference between changing your mind and having a change of heart. He connects an ancient royal tragedy to the quiet epidemic happening in churches, communities, and families right now, and the picture he paints is both unsettling and strangely hopeful. Along the way, he shares some surprisingly candid moments from his own life and the lives of people he loves, and the honesty of it lands harder than any polished argument could.

Hit play and find out why guarding something invisible might be the most urgent thing you do today.

title: An Everyday Faith
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and the life you actually want isn't a lack of willpower or discipline, but a completely wrong idea about how faith is supposed to work? And what if the pressure you've been putting on yourself has been unnecessary this whole time?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin from Harvest Church takes an honest look at why so many of us feel stuck, overwhelmed, or quietly exhausted in our spiritual lives. He gets into the gap between who we want to be and where we actually are, and explores what it really looks like to follow Jesus not as a goal to achieve or a box to tick, but as something lived out one ordinary day at a time. Along the way, he unpacks a familiar prayer that most people have heard but few have sat with long enough to notice what it's actually saying about daily surrender, daily struggle, and daily provision.

Hit play and find out why the single day you're in right now might matter more than you think.

title: Return, Rebuild, Renew - The Book of Ezra
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What do you do when everything you've built has been taken from you, and you're finally given the chance to start again?** Most people would expect to begin with nothing. But what if the very people who took everything were the ones footing the bill to rebuild it?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up the book of Ezra, a corner of the Bible most people have never visited, and finds a story that is far stranger and more compelling than anyone expects. A captive nation, a pagan king with an unlikely nudge from God, and a rebuilding project that nobody should have been able to afford. But woven through the history and the genealogies is something that reaches right into the present: questions about resistance, resolve, identity, and what it actually looks like to return to something you thought was gone for good. This one moves between ancient Babylon and everyday life faster than you'd think possible.

Hit play and find out what the book of Ezra has to say about the life you are trying to rebuild right now.

title: Beauty for Ashes
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What do you do when the life you had looks nothing like the life you're living now? And what if the very thing that feels like the end is actually the beginning of something you couldn't have seen coming?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge shares something she almost didn't preach. Starting with an honest look at a year marked by loss, grief, and unexpected change, she traces a thread from ancient ruins to a simple drive past scorched bushland, and finds a promise tucked inside one of the oldest books of the Bible. What unfolds is a surprisingly tender exploration of what it looks like when hope shows up in the last place you'd think to look for it, and what it might cost you to hold onto the rubble instead.

Press play and let this one sit with you.

title: Rediscovering the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Ps Andrew takes us on a discovery of the Holy Spirit. Who He is, What He does and how we are baptised.

title: Life and Light
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
In this sermon we explore some big concepts about who Jesus is through the book of John 1:1-5

You will be blessed to know He is your life and light!

title: Christmas Eve at Harvest Church
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Join us for a beautiful evening of carols, worship, fun and games as well as a powerful Gospel message about Christ the King.

title: Don't Drink the Poison
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**Don't Drink the Poison**

What if the thing holding you back from real freedom isn't your circumstances, your past, or even the person who hurt you? What if it's something you're choosing to hold onto every single day?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets into something most of us would rather avoid, especially around Christmas. He starts with a question the whole room has to answer honestly, and from there he unpacks why so many people, including church people, find themselves quietly stuck, carrying an old wound from years ago like it happened yesterday. There's a moment in this sermon where a single paragraph gets read aloud and the room goes silent, because everyone recognises themselves in it. That moment alone is worth pressing play for.

Hit play and find out why forgiving someone might be the most self-interested thing you ever do.

title: Come to the Table
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge, Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Join us for a powerful sermon exploring the profound significance of the table in Scripture as a place of reconciliation and unity. Discover how the early church, amidst a backdrop of division and tension, demonstrated radical equality at the table through the unifying power of the Gospel. This message delves into stories of biblical reconciliation, such as Joseph and his brothers, David and Mephibosheth, and Jesus' interactions during the Last Supper. Be inspired by the table's symbolism as a place of grace, restoration, and forgiveness, culminating in the ultimate table of reconciliation—the cross. We invite you to partake in communion and embrace the healing and unity offered through Christ. Don't miss this transformative journey of acceptance, forgiveness, and renewal.

title: But, This I Know
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
**But, This I Know**

What do you do when you are being pressed for answers you simply do not have? What happens when the questions being thrown at you are bigger than anything you can explain?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin unpacks a moment in John chapter 9 that is easy to overlook but surprisingly hard to shake. A man who spent his whole life blind gets caught in the middle of a religious controversy he never asked for, and the only thing he can fall back on is the one thing he knows for certain. What starts as a story about a miracle quickly becomes something much more personal, about the difference between knowing facts and knowing someone, and why that distinction matters more than most of us realise. Ps Caleb is honest about uncertainty, refreshingly funny, and gets to something real about what it looks like to keep moving when you do not have all the answers.

Press play and find out what the formerly blind man knew that the religious experts could not argue with.

title: What are you building?
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What are you actually building with your life? Not your career, your reputation, or your weekend plans, but the thing underneath all of that, the foundation?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a question that sounds simple on the surface and follows it somewhere unexpected. Starting with one of the most familiar passages in the Bible, he unpacks why hearing the right things is not enough, and why the gap between knowing and doing might be the most important distance any of us ever has to close. Along the way, he brings in an ancient blueprint for a flourishing life that is surprisingly straightforward, and asks some honest questions about what is actually shaping you from the inside out.

Hit play and find out what your life is standing on.

title: Socially Acceptable
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: "Are we desensitised to 'socially acceptable sins'? Proverbs 6:16-19 reminds us that what society normalises may still grieve God's heart. From gossip to greed, this message challenges us to examine our lives, repent, and align with God's standards. Let's pursue revival through holiness and prayer, keeping our eyes on Christ—the ultimate antidote to sin."

title: Do Not Resist the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**Do Not Resist the Holy Spirit**

What if the thing you've been most cautious about in your faith is actually the thing you need most? And what if your caution isn't wisdom, but resistance?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a sharp turn from his planned message because sometimes the most honest thing a preacher can do is follow where he's being led. He unpacks why so many people, including committed churchgoers, quietly push back against the Holy Spirit, through their habits, their theology, their sin, and even their comfort. Along the way, he draws on some surprising moments from Scripture and from his own experience that will make you rethink what you thought you knew about how God moves. This one doesn't let you sit on the fence.

Hit play and find out what you might have been resisting without even realising it.

title: UGANDA MISSIONS TEAM WRAP
blurb: Hear all of the amazing things we saw and experienced in Uganda

title: Month of Prayer - Revival
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Are we truly hungry for God? Psalm 63:1 reminds us of David's deep thirst for God's presence. Revival begins with conviction, repentance, and prayer. Acts 2 shows the power of unity and hunger for God. What are we willing to sacrifice for revival? Let's make prayer central and seek Him wholeheartedly.

title: Month of Prayer - Radical Devotion
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back from a deeper faith isn't doubt or circumstances, but simply comfort? And what if the very season you feel like pulling back is actually the moment you're being called forward?

In this episode, Ps Keith Ainge brings a grounded and honest conversation about what it really looks like to step outside the ordinary and say yes when it costs you something. He shares from his own life, including a moment on a drive home that quietly redirected everything, and unpacks why following closely after Jesus is less about spiritual heroics and more about a decision anyone can make. There are questions raised here that most people quietly carry but rarely hear addressed out loud, and the answers might surprise you.

Press play and find out what radical devotion actually looks like when it shows up in a real life.

title: Month of Prayer - Renewal
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been trying to fix about yourself isn't something willpower or self-improvement can actually touch? What if the kind of change you're really looking for requires something you can't manufacture on your own?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge walks through a surprisingly honest list of signs that we might be running on empty spiritually, and most of us will recognise more than one. She draws on one of the most raw and personal poems in all of ancient literature, written by a man who had everything and still found himself completely hollow inside, to explore what genuine renewal actually looks like and what it costs. It's not a guilt trip, and it's not a pep talk. It's something more honest than either of those things.

Hit play and find out what it really takes to start again.

title: Month of Prayer - Repentance
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the part of the Bible you've been quoting your whole life is missing the most important piece? And what if getting what you're hoping for depends entirely on something most people skip over?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up a familiar passage from the book of Joel and finds something hiding in plain sight. He traces a pattern that runs through some of the most dramatic stories in the Old Testament, a cycle that turns out to look uncomfortably familiar in our own lives and in our culture today. There's a kids' relay race, some stolen chocolate, and a moment where the connection between ancient Judah and modern Australia lands in a way you won't see coming. This is not a tidy, comfortable conversation about spirituality. It's an honest look at what we've been avoiding and why it matters more than we think.

Press play and find out what actually comes before the part everyone wants.

title: Our Father
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the way you've been thinking about prayer has been making it harder than it needs to be? And what if the distance you feel from God has less to do with him, and more to do with a misunderstanding that goes all the way back to the beginning?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge shares a story from his childhood that reframes everything about how we approach God. You'll hear why most people quietly struggle with prayer, what a torn curtain has to do with your everyday life, and how two small words at the start of the most famous prayer ever prayed might completely shift the way you see yourself and God. This one starts somewhere unexpected and ends up somewhere worth going.

Hit play and find out what those two words actually mean for you.

title: The Heart of an Armour Bearer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Are you ready to embrace the heart of an armor bearer? Inspired by 1 Samuel 14, this message challenges us to step out in faith, trust God, and move in unity. Just as Jonathan's armor bearer said, 'I am with you, heart and soul,' we're called to support one another and see God do extraordinary things through us.

title: Armour Bearers
speaker: Ps David McCracken
blurb: Ps David spoke prophetically over the life, direction and future of our church as well as brought insight to many individuals. The overall theme, armour bearers release the victory. This is an important word for Harvest Church

title: How to Talk about Jesus
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: We're reminded of our calling to share the good news of Jesus with others. This message emphasizes the importance of personal evangelism, rooted in Isaiah 6:8 - 'Here I am. Send me.' We're all called to be evangelists in our daily lives, not just those with a specific gift. The main barriers to sharing our faith often stem from fear - fear of inadequacy, losing reputation, rejection, or appearing hypocritical. To overcome these, we're encouraged to follow Jesus' example of compassion and love for others. The message outlines five key components for effective evangelism: prayer, loving others, sharing the gospel message, telling our personal story, and being obedient despite the results. We're reminded that our job is to sow seeds, while God brings the harvest.

title: Life Lessons from Golf
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this engaging exploration, we're challenged to examine our integrity through the lens of golf and biblical stories. Joseph's unwavering integrity in the face of temptation from Potiphar's wife serves as a powerful example. We're reminded that integrity often comes at a cost, but ultimately leads to greater rewards. The message emphasizes that our true character is revealed when no one is watching, drawing parallels between the hidden moments on a golf course and our daily lives. We're encouraged to 'take the penalty' and do what's right, even when it's difficult, trusting that God sees our hearts and will honor our faithfulness.

title: Great Faith
speaker: Ps Matt Heins
blurb: In this powerful message, we're reminded of the importance of cultivating great faith in our lives. The story of Joseph from Genesis 43 serves as a backdrop to illustrate how we can sometimes get caught up in 'donkey mentalities' - focusing on small, insignificant issues while missing God's bigger picture. We're encouraged to shift our perspective, understanding that God is always moving in our lives, even when we can't see it. The message emphasizes the need to activate our faith through prayer and immersion in God's Word, reminding us that God delights not only in our worship but also in our requests. This teaching challenges us to maintain a healthy disconnect from constant discouragement, drawing inspiration from biblical figures who persevered through trials. As we reflect on these insights, we're inspired to nurture a faith that's ready for the big things God has in store for us.

title: Holy Spirit Fire
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been missing in your faith isn't more knowledge, more discipline, or more effort? What if it's something you can't manufacture on your own, no matter how hard you try?

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes you on a journey through some of the most vivid and unexpected moments in Scripture, from a bizarre ancient covenant ceremony involving split animals, to a shepherd who almost walked straight past the most important conversation of his life. Along the way, he builds a case for something that quietly challenges the way most of us think about what it means to follow Jesus. This isn't a tidy theological lecture. It's honest, a little raw, and at times surprisingly funny.

Press play and find out what the fire of the Holy Spirit actually has to do with your everyday life.

title: The Lord is Near
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this powerful exploration of Philippians 4, we're reminded of the transformative power of joy and contentment in our Christian walk. The central message revolves around the profound truth that 'the Lord is near.' This simple yet profound statement serves as the foundation for overcoming anxiety, finding peace, and living a life of rejoicing. We're encouraged to shift our focus from worldly concerns to the presence of God, bringing all our worries to Him in prayer with thanksgiving. This practice unlocks a peace that surpasses all understanding, guarding our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus. The message challenges us to examine how we interpret and apply Scripture, urging us to consider the full context rather than isolated verses. It's a call to root our contentment and joy not in circumstances, but in our relationship with Christ.

title: Tackling The Tensions
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb: In this powerful message, we explore the concept of divine tensions in our faith journey. We're reminded that not all tension is negative - in fact, it's often necessary for growth and strength. Just as a suspension bridge needs tension to function, our spiritual lives often require us to hold seemingly contradictory truths in balance. The Bible itself is full of these 'divine tensions' or paradoxes - like being both a new creation and still being transformed, or experiencing both suffering and glory. Rather than seeing these as contradictions, we're encouraged to approach them with curiosity and humility, like Moses approaching the burning bush. By using our 'spiritual eyes' and stepping closer to investigate, we may find that these tensions are actually holy ground where God reveals Himself to us.

title: Uncomfortable Comfortability
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and the life you actually want isn't a lack of faith or effort, but something you've been holding onto so tightly you've stopped noticing it's even there? And what if the cost of letting go feels so heavy that even a genuinely good person could walk away from the best thing they've ever been offered?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin opens up a familiar Bible story and finds something uncomfortable sitting right at the centre of it. He explores why so many of us can be passionate, sincere, and genuinely hungry for more, and still find ourselves stuck in the same place. You might recognise yourself in the story more than you expect, and the areas where we get stuck might be closer to home than you'd like to admit.

Hit play and find out what it might be costing you to stay comfortable.

title: Citizens of Heaven
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: We are not from this world! We have an eternal and heavenly citienship

title: No Turning Back
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back from the future you want isn't a lack of faith or effort, but the fact that you keep looking the wrong direction? And what if that pattern is older and more human than you ever realised?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge walks through two contrasting stories, one from ancient history and one from the writings of a man who lost everything and called it the best thing that ever happened to him. Along the way, he uses baseball, a DeLorean, and a pillar of salt to explore something that most of us do without even noticing: dragging the past into the future and wondering why we never seem to arrive. This is not a guilt trip and it is not a pep talk. It is something more honest than either of those things.

Hit play and find out what it actually looks like to stop looking back.

title: Heavenly Wisdom above Earthly Knowledge
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Join us as we explore together the book of Philippians with Ps Andrew Cartledge

title: Working Out Salvation
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Here are the show notes for this episode:

Most of us spend our lives trying to climb higher, get noticed, and secure our place. But what if the path to something better actually runs in the opposite direction?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most misunderstood tensions in the Christian life: the gap between what we say we believe and how we actually live it out. Drawing from the book of Philippians, he unpacks why unity keeps falling apart, what humility actually costs, and why a donkey illustration might be one of the most honest descriptions of how Christians treat each other you will ever hear. There is also a surprising look at a literary device buried in an ancient letter that changes the way you see the entire story of Jesus.

Press play and see where this one takes you.

title: Joy in Suffering
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you're most desperate to escape is actually the thing that moves you forward? And what if the secret to joy isn't found in comfort, but somewhere far less expected?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up the Book of Philippians and takes us inside the story of a man writing about joy from a prison cell. Before he gets to the good stuff, he lays some groundwork about how we read the Bible that might just change the way you've been approaching it your whole life. There's history, there's context, and there's a thread running through it all that connects ancient suffering to something deeply relevant right now.

Hit play and find out why the worst thing that happened to Paul might be the reason you're encouraged today.

title: Travel Light
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing weighing you down most isn't meant to be yours to carry at all? And what if letting it go has less to do with willpower and more to do with who you actually believe is holding the other end?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge shares a sermon that started not in a pulpit but in the middle of a sleepless night, Bible in hand, with a familiar verse suddenly hitting very differently. She takes a closer look at a single Greek word from 1 Peter 5 that reframes what it actually means to hand something over, and why most of us quietly take it back before anything can change. Along the way, she builds a picture of the kind of God you are supposedly trusting with your heaviest stuff, and the portrait is more specific and more compelling than you might expect.

If you have ever prayed something over and then picked it straight back up again, this one is worth your time.

title: On Mission
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the most meaningful thing you could do this week cost less than a cup of coffee? And what if the church you attend in a small Australian country town was somehow connected to children in Kolkata, farmers in Georgia, and street kids in Lesotho?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes Harvest Church through what it actually means to be a church that looks beyond its own walls. He gets into the uncomfortable questions about why any local church should care about what happens on the other side of the world, and he does not let the audience off the hook easily. You will hear stories that are hard to forget, meet some remarkable people doing extraordinary things in places most of us will never visit, and find yourself rethinking what it means to be part of something bigger than your own backyard.

Hit play and find out what it looks like when a regional church in Victoria takes seriously the idea that the whole world is its neighbourhood.

title: Pentecost Sunday
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been told is too confusing, too chaotic, or just "not for you" is actually the very thing you've been missing? And what if the reason it feels so distant is simply because nobody has taken the time to explain it properly?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes one of the most misunderstood topics in the Christian faith and lays it out in a way that is honest, grounded, and genuinely surprising. He traces a thread from ancient Jewish festivals all the way to a room full of praying people waiting for something they had never seen before, and then connects that moment directly to your everyday life. There is more here than tongues and fire. There are four markers that Ps Andrew unpacks that most Pentecostal churches rarely talk about, and at least one of them will probably catch you off guard.

Press play and find out what it actually means to be filled with something you cannot see.

title: Just One Small Jar Of Oil
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What do you do when everything you had is gone and all you're left with is something so small it barely seems worth mentioning? And what if that tiny, seemingly insignificant thing is actually exactly what's needed?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes an ancient story from the book of Second Kings and opens it up in a way that feels surprisingly personal and immediate. She brings her own moments of feeling completely out of her depth, as a mum, as a student, as someone standing in front of a room wondering if she has anything worth giving. What unfolds is a conversation about what happens when we stop pretending we have it together and bring our nothing to the table instead. This is not a tidy, triumphant story. It is honest, warm, and at times unexpectedly funny.

Press play and find out what a small jar of oil has to do with the life you are actually living right now.

title: Joy in the Spirit
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if joy has nothing to do with how good your life is going right now? And what if the people who seem to have it figured out are facing the exact same struggles you are?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin takes an honest look at what joy actually is, and what it is not. He gets into the gap between the kind of happiness the world chases and something far more grounded, something that holds up when life gets hard. Through a handful of unexpectedly funny personal stories and some passages from the Bible that hit differently in context, Caleb builds a case for why real joy might be less about feeling good and more about what you know to be true. This one gets personal toward the end, and that is where it gets genuinely interesting.

Hit play and find out why knowing the outcome changes everything.

title: Gospel Participants
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if becoming part of something bigger than yourself was less about what you believe and more about what you actually do with that belief? And what if the gap between those two things is exactly where most people get stuck?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up Philippians 1 and explores what it really means to be included in something you did not earn, commissioned for something you cannot ignore, and still being shaped into someone you have not yet become. There is a thread running through this passage that connects identity, purpose, and promise in a way that might quietly challenge some assumptions you have carried for a long time. If you have ever wondered whether faith is just a destination or something more like an ongoing renovation, this conversation is worth your time.

Hit play and see where this takes you.

title: Power of Pentecost
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing most Christians claim to believe in is also the thing they understand least? And what if that gap between belief and understanding is exactly what's holding them back?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the most misunderstood moments in the entire Christian story, the day that changed everything and set in motion something that is still unfolding today. He explores what was actually happening in that upper room, why it mattered then, and what it means for ordinary people living ordinary lives right now. You will hear some ideas that might surprise you, some that might challenge you, and at least one that might make you rethink something you thought you already had figured out.

Press play and find out what you might have been missing.

title: Light It Up
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the very thing the world needs most is already inside you, and you've just been keeping it hidden? And what if that's not just a nice idea, but something you've actually been commissioned to do?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a familiar phrase from the Sermon on the Mount and unpacks what it actually means to be called the light of the world. Not as a metaphor to feel good about, but as a responsibility that changes how you live every single day. She explores what the moon has to do with your faith, why darkness never stands a chance, and what it looks like when Christians stop treating their role in the world as an optional extra. There's a moment in here involving a nearly empty petrol tank on a dark highway that will stick with you longer than you might expect.

Hit play and find out what Jesus really meant when he looked at ordinary people and said, you are the light.

title: It Is Well
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What do you do when the thing you hoped for finally arrives, only to be taken away? And what do you say to the people around you when everything inside you is falling apart?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest look at what happens when life does not deliver what we expected, and how we respond when disappointment cuts deeper than just a bad day. Drawing from an often overlooked story tucked away in the Old Testament, he traces the journey of a woman who faced loss in layers, and whose response to each one is surprising, even unsettling. There is something in this story about the gap between what we confess and what we feel, and how those two things can exist at the same time without one canceling out the other.

Press play and sit with this one.

title: A Different Spirit
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if two people can look at exactly the same situation, face exactly the same obstacles, and walk away with completely opposite conclusions? And what if the difference between them has nothing to do with strength, skill, or personality?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes us into one of the most gripping moments in the Old Testament, where twelve leaders are sent on the same mission, see the same land, and come back with reports that could not be more different. What set one man apart from the rest is not what you might expect, and the question Ps Rachel builds toward is deeply personal: which kind of spirit do you actually have? This is a sermon that challenges you to look honestly at what you focus on, what you remember, and what you really believe when the odds feel stacked against you.

Hit play and find out what it means to carry a different spirit.

title: Passion of the Church
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What does it actually look like to live with genuine passion, not just talk about it? And what happens when the thing you're meant to care most about starts to feel routine, comfortable, and safe?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge walks through one of the most striking moments in the Gospel of Mark, where Jesus is out ahead of the crowd on the road to Jerusalem, and something about the way he is walking stops people in their tracks. What was it that the crowd could sense? And what does that moment have to do with the way you and I are living right now? This sermon pulls together big questions about sacrifice, identity, and what we actually value, weaving in some unexpected moments of humour and honesty that make the hard stuff land in a real way. There is something here for anyone who has ever wondered whether faith is supposed to feel like more than this.

Press play and find out what it looks like to stop just going through the motions.

title: Passion of the Cross
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if everything you thought greatness looked like was completely backwards? And what if the people closest to Jesus made the exact same mistake you might be making right now?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the more confronting moments in the gospel of Mark, where Jesus makes a shocking prediction, his disciples completely miss the point, and then get caught red-handed arguing about something that reveals a lot more about human nature than most of us are comfortable admitting. There is a reason Jesus had to say the same thing three times, and understanding why tells you something important about how we all think and what it actually takes to change. This one moves between ancient roads in Galilee and the very modern pressures of comparison, status, and what we secretly believe makes someone worth something.

Hit play and find out what Jesus said greatness actually looks like.

title: Passion of the Christ
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been told to chase, passion, is actually pointing you toward something you've been avoiding? And what if the version of passion that matters most isn't about feeling anything at all?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a word we think we understand and turns it completely inside out. He traces three very different kinds of passion, from the desires that quietly pull us off course, to the widespread numbness that has settled over everyday life, to something far older and more costly than either. What he uncovers in the Gospel of Mark is not what most people expect when they hear the word "passion," and that surprise is exactly the point. If you've ever felt like you're just going through the motions, or wondered why your faith feels like it's running on empty, this conversation is going to get under your skin.

Hit play and find out why the passion that changes everything looks nothing like what you'd expect.

title: Open
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if you were given a message to deliver, knowing in advance that no one would listen? And what if that same problem turned out to be less about the audience, and more about you?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the strangest and most unsettling passages in the Bible, a moment where God sends a prophet with a message that seems almost designed to fail. But as Andrew unpacks the thread running from Isaiah through to Jesus and the New Testament, something unexpected emerges about what it actually takes to hear, see, and receive what God is saying. It is not the message that needs to change. It is the condition of the person receiving it. This episode asks some honest questions about what it looks like when our hearts, eyes, and ears are closed without us even realising it.

Hit play and find out what it means to be truly open.
